analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/reference/configuration.md, line 685. The row for DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS now says the variable is 'Forwarded to the launchd provider job' instead of 'Not forwarded to LaunchAgents'. The visible units are base text only, covering lines 1-485 and 307-485. The edited line 685 falls outside the supplied base excerpts, so I judged it from the patch hunk alone. Relevant threat: T-041 (prefix-cache SSD tier, A-001).

The documented change means that an operator who disables incremental checkpoints with a negative value (0, false, no, off) now has that setting reach installed daemons. Previously those daemons ran with the default (on). This makes the knob more effective and does not widen the at-rest surface. It only selects delta versus full checkpoint writes, and the DBK3 crypto, HMAC lookup tags, sliding TTL, salt scoping and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch are untouched. There is no new attack surface here and no weakening of a mitigation.

Open integration question: the doc now claims LaunchAgent.swift (passthroughEnvKeys) forwards this variable. That Swift change is not in the supplied units, and I cannot verify it. If the code change is in the same PR, the next pass should confirm only that the allow-list adds this single key and that the value is parsed as a negative-disable boolean. If the code does not forward the variable, this is a documentation-accuracy issue only. The base text I could read, such as the Local GLM section and the add-on hold section, is unchanged and out of scope. I identified no regression.
